items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: There was just a handful, like Stan Getz and Zoot

ctx.x: I have to confess that I had some help from my family. I was making a living but I was doing better than if I was just playing the music with my family’s help. Because the only white guys I know that were making a living, there were very few white musicians who

actually made a living just playing jazz. In other words, guys like Al Cohn and Johnny Mandel, a whole school of guys, they were doing commercial work. Arranging or playing all kinds of studio dates. They became studio musicians. There was just a handful, like Stan Getz and Zoot, who didn’t want, I mean he was the exception because he was a true Bohemian or whatever they called them.
And those guys would often times, wouldn’t they just tour as soloists and play with—
